**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** A Corrupted Mind

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Paduṭṭhacitta Sutta* (Iti 20; PTS It 12) is a short discourse located in the first chapter of the *Itivuttaka* in the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The core teaching of the sutta explains that having a corrupted mind (*paduṭṭhacitta*) leads an individual to rebirth in the lower realms or planes of deprivation [SuttaCentral]. The text has been translated into multiple modern languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

SuttaCentral notes a curated full Chinese parallel at T 765.4, a passage-level parallel in the Aṅguttara Nikāya at AN 1.43, and records its citation in the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37, *Sāsanapaṭṭhāna*) [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus corroborates these connections: the longest shared passage is with the *Sāsanapaṭṭhāna* of the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37, §2.1–6.1 ↔ §29.1–33.1), along with an extensive match in the *Ekakanipāta* of the Aṅguttara Nikāya (AN 1, §2.1–2.5 ↔ §42.1.7–43.1.5) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects substantial internal reuse across the *Itivuttaka*, exhibiting a nearly complete parallel structure with the *Pasannacitta Sutta* (Iti 21, §0.1–6.2 ↔ §0.1–6.2), as well as formulaic overlaps with Iti 11, Iti 64, Iti 66, Iti 99, the *Mahāsīhanāda Sutta* (MN 12), and the *Nettivibhāvinī* [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matching, DharmaNexus aligns passages of the text with a Tibetan canonical discourse (BO_K10_D0338_H0343) and the Chinese *Ekottarika-āgama* (增壹阿含經, T 125, fascicle 44) [DharmaNexus].

None of the matched passages in the reference literature analyze this discourse directly; instead, they treat the lexical compound *paduṭṭhacitta* in general contexts or cite unrelated canonical verses such as the *Sattabhariyā Sutta* (AN 7.63) and Jātaka stories.
